title: Documentation, Life-Cycle, Change and Configuration Management

header.html: 3.1 Explain the purpose of organizational processes and procedures: documentation (physical vs logical diagrams, rack diagrams, cable maps, network diagrams at layers 1, 2 and 3, asset inventory, IP address management, SLA, wireless survey and heat map); life-cycle management (EOL, EOS, software management, decommissioning); change management; configuration management (production, backup, baseline or golden configuration)
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1Documentation

Document Purpose
Physical diagram Where equipment and cables physically are
Logical diagram How data flows: IP addresses, VLANs, routing, zones
Rack diagram Which device sits in which rack unit
Cable map / diagram Where each cable runs and its labels
Network diagrams by layer Layer 1 (cabling), layer 2 (switches, VLANs), layer 3 (subnets, routing)
Asset inventory Hardware, software, licensing and warranty support records
IP address management (IPAM) A tool that tracks subnets, addresses and DHCP/DNS usage
Service-level agreement (SLA) A contract defining expected service, uptime and response times
Wireless survey / heat map Maps signal strength and coverage of the Wi-Fi
Exam tip

. Physical diagram = where things are. Logical diagram = how traffic flows. A heat map shows wireless coverage gaps.

2Life-cycle management

Term Meaning
End-of-life (EOL) The vendor stops selling the product
End-of-support (EOS) The vendor stops patches and support; plan replacement before this date
Software management Patches and bug fixes, OS updates, firmware updates, applied with testing and a rollback plan
Decommissioning Safely retiring a device: remove from service, wipe data and configuration, update inventory and documentation, dispose responsibly

3Change management

A formal process that makes changes safe and traceable: request (service request tracking), assessment of risk and impact, approval, scheduling in a maintenance window, implementation with a rollback plan, testing, and documentation.

4Configuration management

Configuration Meaning
Production configuration What the device is running now
Backup configuration A saved copy used to restore a failed or replaced device
Baseline / golden configuration The approved standard used to build and compare devices; drift from the baseline is investigated
Exam tip

. EOL means no longer sold; EOS means no longer supported. Plan replacement before end-of-support.

Exam tip

. Golden configuration = approved standard; backup configuration = restore copy; production = what runs now.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A technician needs to see which VLANs and subnets exist and how they connect. Which document helps?

  • AA rack diagram
  • BA logical network diagram
  • CA cable map
  • DA warranty record
Show the answer

Answer: B. Logical diagrams show addressing and traffic flow.

S2A vendor announces it will no longer provide security patches for a switch model after a date. What is this called?

  • AEnd-of-life
  • BA baseline configuration
  • CDecommissioning
  • DEnd-of-support
Show the answer

Answer: D. EOS means the vendor stops patches and support.

S3A new router is being built. Which configuration provides the approved standard to start from?

  • AThe golden (baseline) configuration
  • BThe production configuration of another site
  • CA backup from a failed device
  • DA factory default
Show the answer

Answer: A. The baseline is the approved standard.

S4Wi-Fi users in one corner complain of weak signal. Which document best shows the problem?

  • AA rack diagram
  • BAn IPAM export
  • CA wireless heat map
  • DAn SLA
Show the answer

Answer: C. Heat maps show coverage and signal strength.

S5Which step comes first in a formal change management process?

  • AImplementation on the production device
  • BPost-change testing
  • CDecommissioning the old device
  • DA documented change request with risk assessment
Show the answer

Answer: D. Changes start with a request and impact assessment.

S6Which tool tracks subnets and addresses to avoid conflicts?

  • AA cable map
  • BIP address management
  • CA patch panel
  • DA wireless survey
Show the answer

Answer: B. IPAM manages address allocation.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What does EOL mean?

Show the answer

The vendor stops selling the product.

R2What does EOS mean?

Show the answer

The vendor stops providing patches and support.

R3What is a rack diagram?

Show the answer

A diagram of which device occupies which rack unit.

R4What is a golden configuration?

Show the answer

The approved baseline configuration used to build and compare devices.

R5Name one decommissioning step.

Show the answer

For example wipe the data and update the inventory.

R6What does an SLA define?

Show the answer

Expected service levels such as uptime and response times.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Documents physical vs logical; rack, cable, layer 1/2/3 diagrams; inventory; IPAM; SLA; heat map
Life-cycle EOL (not sold), EOS (no support); patches, firmware; decommissioning
Change request, assess, approve, schedule, implement with rollback, test, document
Configurations production, backup, golden baseline
